Understanding MLB Odds and Betting Lines

Explore MLB odds, lines, popular betting events, and frequently asked questions with DraftKings for the 2026/27 MLB season.

How To Read MLB Odds?

MLB odds indicate potential payouts using the (+) and (-) symbols to represent the odds.

The opening line is the first betting line for an MLB game. Opening lines can change as more bets are placed and new information becomes available, such as starting pitcher announcements, injuries, lineup changes, or weather updates.

A typical MLB odds sheet may look something like this:

Team

	

Run Line

	

Over/Under Totals

	

Moneyline Odds




New York

	

-1.5 / +135

	

8.5 / -110 - O

	

-145




Boston

	

+1.5 / -155

	

8.5 / -110 - U

	

+125

Moneylines, run lines, and over/under totals can all show a positive (+) or negative (-) odds indicator.

A quick way to understand American odds is to look at the plus or minus sign.

The (+) represents the underdog and shows how much a $100 winning bet would earn in profit. For example, a $100 bet on a +125 underdog would win $125, for a total payout of $225.

The (-) represents the favorite and shows how much you need to wager to win $100 in profit. For example, a -145 favorite means you would need to wager $145 to win $100.

In either case, if your bet wins, you also receive your original stake back.

You don't have to bet exactly $100 or the amount shown in the odds. Using $100 simply makes it easier to understand the potential payout.

For example, a $20 bet on a +125 underdog would win $25 in profit, for a total payout of $45. A $29 bet on a -145 favorite would win approximately $20 in profit, for a total payout of approximately $49.

What are the types of MLB Bets?

You can bet on various aspects of a MLB game or season using spreads, moneylines, futures, and player props. Learn more about the types of MLB bets that suit you, and have fun. With several ways to bet on MLB and add excitement to the game, it’s no wonder MLB betting is so popular among sports fans. 

What are MLB spreads or run lines?

A point spread, also known as a runline in baseball, is the amount by which a team is favored to win. Runlines are commonly set at 1.5. However, DraftKings allows alternative lines that are based on the matchup. If you think your favorite team is going to win big on a given day, bet on them to beat the spread! 

If a team is listed as +1.5, it means they are the underdog. For example, if the Toronto Blue Jays are playing the New York Mets, and the Blue Jays are listed at -1.5, they need to win by two or more runs to cover the spread. If the Mets are listed at +1.5, they need to either lose by just one run or win the game to cover the spread.

What are MLB moneylines?

An MLB moneyline bet is a bet on which team will win the game outright. The margin of victory doesn’t matter, only the final result. Each team is assigned moneyline odds, which determine the potential payout for a winning bet. Favorites typically have negative odds, while underdogs typically have positive odds.

What are MLB three-way moneylines?

A three-way moneyline gives three possible outcomes to bet on: Team A wins, Team B wins, or the two teams tie. Three-way moneylines are bets on nine innings, since a MLB game can’t end in a tie. If the two teams are tied after nine innings, it’s considered a tie for the three-way moneyline bet, and the winner in extra innings doesn’t matter.

What are MLB over/under bets?

Also known as Totals, MLB over/under bets focus on the total score of teams in the individual MLB game. For example, if the over/under of the Mets vs. Blue Jays game is set at 8.5, that means the teams would have to score a combined nine runs or more to be considered over. Eight or less and the under bettors are winners.

What are MLB player props?

Player prop bets are wagers on a specific MLB player’s performance in a game. For example, betting on if a player hits a home run in any given game.MLB player props available on DraftKings may vary by game and jurisdiction. Depending on availability, MLB player props may include:

Batter props: Bet on individual aspects of a batter's performance, including home runs, hits, total bases, RBIs, and stolen bases.

Home runs: Pick whether a specific batter will hit a home run during the game.

Hits: Bet on whether a batter will record a certain number of hits in a game.

Total bases: Wager on the number of total bases a batter will record, with singles, doubles, triples, and home runs each counting toward the total.

RBIs: Bet on whether a batter will record a certain number of runs batted in during the game.

Stolen bases: Pick whether a player will record a stolen base during the game.

Pitcher props: Follow a starting pitcher's performance with wagers on stats such as strikeouts and outs recorded.

Strikeouts: Bet on whether a pitcher will record a certain number of strikeouts during the game.

Outs recorded: Wager on how many outs a pitcher will record before leaving the game.

To record a win: Pick whether a pitcher will “record a win” for the game.

What are MLB parlay bets?

In a parlay, two or more bets are combined into a single wager. All selections in the parlay must win for the parlay to win. Adding more selections changes the odds and can increase the potential payout.

Parlays can include all kinds of bets, such as runlines, moneylines, or over/unders. Check out our How to Bet 101 guide for an example of a parlay bet.

What are MLB futures?

MLB futures are wagers on the entire season, or remainder of the season if it's in progress. The most popular MLB futures bet is who will win the World Series. Futures typically pay well because it’s tough to select a winner months in advance. A lot can change in a season, from trades to injuries. The beauty of futures is they add excitement to the overall season instead of a single game, so you can remain invested all season long.

What are the Biggest MLB Betting Events?
World Series

There are no games bigger in baseball than the World Series. The annual, best-of-seven series crowns the greatest team in the Major League, and games are tense, action-packed, and filled with emotion. Make the biggest event in the sport even more exciting with a wager.

MLB Playoffs

To get to the World Series, MLB teams need to get through multiple rounds of playoffs. With rivalries and elimination on the line, these multi-game series are some of the best games baseball has to offer.

MLB Regular Season

You can bet on MLB regular season games with DraftKings and find a variety of ways to add excitement to every game. Regular season games help determine which teams make it to the MLB playoffs, giving every matchup added importance as the season progresses. Whether you like following individual players, picking game winners, or looking ahead to the World Series, DraftKings offers several ways to bet on the regular season, including player props, parlays, run lines, moneylines, over/unders, and futures.
